candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Sermo de Domino Nostro
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Sermo de Domino Nostro 7-8 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Sermo de Domino Nostro (c. 363 AD)

'There shall no man see me and live' — and yet Moses sees the Lord's back as he passes by. Ephrem reads the verse as the canonical disclosure that full vision of God is reserved for the Incarnation: only when the Word is made flesh may humanity behold the divine face without being consumed. Tewahedo reads Ex 33:20 and 1 Jn 1:1 ('which we have seen with our eyes') as a single canonical arc from veiled vision to face-to-face Word.

candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos III.14
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.14 (c. 350 AD)

'And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live' — Athanasius marks ou dynēsē idein mou to prosōpon (thou canst not see my face) as the UNSEEABLE-FATHER / VISIBLE-WORD distinction. The Father-in-his-essence is unseeable (1 Tim 6:16 oude idein tis dynatai); what Moses is granted to see (LXX ta opisthia — 'the back parts') is the visible-condescension of the Word-pre-incarnate. Athanasius reads the Word as the agent of EVERY OT theophany (the burning bush, the pillar of cloud, the man-Yahweh at Mamre, the Sinai-glory) — the Father is never seen, only the Word who is the Father's-form-and-image. This hermeneutic grounds the Tewahedo iconographic-convention: the Father is never directly-depicted, only the Word-incarnate.
